clue.text: Offsets the effects of Communist writer needing to satisfy Stalin primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the name is used

blocks.note: a common short form of Communist
a pen is the tool that writes
to sate an appetite is to satisfy it
first letter of the dictator's name

explanation.surface: A Soviet-era writer has to keep Stalin happy to make up for something he has written.
explanation.definitionFit: To compensate for something is to make amends or counterbalance it, cancelling out its effects.

clue.text: Fully equipped to contend for a prize around the end of April

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so these letters wrap the other
the end of points to the final letter only of the month

blocks.note: to compete is to strive to win
last letter of April

explanation.surface: Someone fully kitted out enters a contest that runs to late April.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete with all its parts means having every piece of equipment or fitting needed.

clue.text: Missouri girls making treacle

blocks.note: the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri
lasses are young women, chiefly in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: Girls from Missouri cooking up something syrupy.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the American name for the dark syrup British cooks call treacle, a byproduct of sugar refining.

clue.text: Wear away strip essentially against European opposition opening with Germany and Spain

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the very middle of the word
an opening is the beginning, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
the central letter of the five-letter word
the first letter of opposition
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A football strip worn thin in a European tie, opening against Germany and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' means next to: the middle letter of strip sits beside the European letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear something away gradually, as water and wind do to rock.

clue.text: Cave in Southern Belgium penetrated by university team

indicators.note: something penetrated has another thing pushed inside it, so a letter goes into the pair

blocks.note: S is short for southern
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
U is short for university
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A cave in the south of Belgium is explored by a university team of potholers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' looks like a noun, a hole in the ground; 'Cave in' is a verb phrase meaning collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that subsides sinks or collapses downwards, just as a roof caves in.

clue.text: Flier showing volunteers facing half- hearted moaner

indicators.note: half-hearted means half of the heart is lost, so one of the two central letters goes

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve force
a nagger is someone who complains constantly

explanation.surface: Volunteers confronted by a grumbler who has lost some enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanager is a brightly coloured American songbird, and in crosswords a flier is often any bird.

clue.text: Went, after having no doubt reportedly, for an aquatic perennial

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word counts by its sound

blocks.note: sure means without doubt, and in many accents sounds like the edge of the sea
to go is a euphemism for urinating, so went can mean wee'd

explanation.surface: Someone went, having checked first, for a pond plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Went is coy slang: if you 'went' before a journey, you weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoreweed (Littorella) is a small perennial plant growing at the edges of lakes and ponds, often submerged.

clue.text: Snub Nick

blocks.note: first meaning: to ignore someone deliberately
second meaning: a small gash in the skin

explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a man's name being snubbed; it is a small wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone dead is to ignore them pointedly, and a cut is also a shallow wound or notch.

clue.text: Piece regularly dismissed after endless quote about back of door knocker

indicators.note: letters are sent away at regular intervals, keeping every other one
with no end means the final letter is chopped off
about means surrounding, so the shortened word wraps around a letter
the back of something is its rear, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: to cite is to quote as evidence
the final letter of door
the second and fourth letters of piece

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece cut short after an endless quotation about a door knocker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'door knocker' reads as one object; the definition is just knocker, slang for someone who runs things down.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something is to disparage it, so a knocker is a fault-finder or reviewer who pans things.

clue.text: About to block not this but the other source of danger

indicators.note: to block a passage is to sit in the middle of it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: not this but the other means that
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to stop one thing, not this but the other, which is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not this but the other' is a roundabout way of saying the opposite of this.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is something or someone likely to cause harm, a menace or hazard.

clue.text: Academic, a short time after, left to get port

blocks.note: a Master of Arts, a university graduate
the standard abbreviation for left
a mo is a moment, as in 'just a mo'

explanation.surface: A lecturer leaves for the docks shortly after someone else has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a short time after' places the moment after the letter for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmo is a Swedish seaport on the Oresund strait, facing Copenhagen across the water.

clue.text: Nothing found in lined bra used as an ammunition carrier

indicators.note: something used is worn and battered out of its original shape, so the letters are rearranged
one item is found inside another, so it sits within the other letters

blocks.note: the letters of the two words, to be rearranged
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a padded bra being used to carry bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolier is a belt slung over the shoulder with loops or pockets holding cartridges.

clue.text: Following advice enrol a number on the way back? Grand

indicators.note: travelling on the way back means going in the opposite direction, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: to list is an old sense of to enlist or enrol
one number among many
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to sign up a number of people on a return trip, and thinks it grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is listening heeds what they are told, taking in and acting on the guidance given.

clue.text: Plant last of evidence before broadcast about implicating Colombian leader

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter only of the next word
turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
to implicate someone is to draw them into the matter, so a letter is wrapped inside
a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the country's adjective is taken

blocks.note: the final letter of evidence
to air a programme is to broadcast it
the opening letter of Colombian

explanation.surface: Evidence planted before a news broadcast about a Colombian leader's role in a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb about planting evidence; it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, low flowering shrubs.

clue.text: Fate of criminal once finding work absorbing in that place? On the contrary

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so one word holds another inside it
this reverses the roles just stated, so the holder becomes the one held and vice versa

blocks.note: there means in that place
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Asking whether a convict's fate was to find a job soaking things up somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, work absorbs the place; 'On the contrary' flips it so the place absorbs the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging was formerly the punishment for capital crimes, and 'the rope' is the idiom for execution by hanging.

clue.text: In excess of principal’s expenses

blocks.note: over means more than
a head is a principal of a school; the apostrophe s is read as the plural's s

explanation.surface: A headteacher's spending has gone over budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Overheads are a business's regular running costs, such as rent and heating, as opposed to direct costs.

clue.text: Musician’s vibrator found in study I hear

indicators.note: I hear signals that what follows is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it, and read in the present tense is said like the answer

explanation.surface: A musician's vibrating gadget turns up in someone's study, as rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: In a clarinet, oboe or bassoon a thin cane strip vibrates against the mouthpiece to make the sound.

clue.text: Become pale finding American in fancy toilet cubicle at last

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order
at last points to the final letter only of the preceding word
one thing is found inside another, so a letter sits within the rest

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the last letter of cubicle, joining the rearranged letters
A is short for American

explanation.surface: A visiting American goes white on discovering a fancy toilet cubicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants grown in darkness etiolate, turning pale and spindly; more loosely, a person can lose colour and vigour.

clue.text: Impudence seen on prisoner’s face

blocks.note: a con is a convict
front means cheek or brazenness

explanation.surface: Cheekiness shows on a prisoner's face.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the cheek below, after the prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To face a problem or person is to meet it head on, to confront it.

clue.text: Resolutely oppose ignoring daughter’s support

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to beard someone is to confront them boldly
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Firmly refusing to go along with a daughter's request for backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to hold it up, carry its weight, or sustain it.

clue.text: Copy in Erica struggling to grasp programming language

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
to grasp is to hold within one's hand, so the name wraps around the other letters

blocks.note: the letters of the name, to be rearranged
PL, as in PL/I, is a short form of programming language

explanation.surface: Erica, a student, struggles to understand a programming language and copies the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an original object, such as a model or facsimile.

clue.text: Excessive to intervene in free love as a public entertainment in the past

definitions.text: a public entertainment in the past

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so these letters go into the middle of the others

blocks.note: to rid is to free from something
OTT is over the top
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Overdoing things interferes with free love as a spectacle of times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridotto was an eighteenth-century public assembly with music and dancing, often masked, held in Venice and London.

clue.text: Priest interrupting continually sent up with ease

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means moved upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top
interrupting means breaking into, so the name goes inside the other word

blocks.note: ever means always
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A priest keeps breaking in, mocked with careless ease.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve pain or worry is to lessen it, making it easier to bear.

clue.text: Cunning Conservative joins party on the rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: C is short for Conservative
a revel is a lively celebration

explanation.surface: A wily Tory signs up to a political party whose fortunes are improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a political party; it is a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning person is clever in a sly or ingenious way, shrewd and quick-witted.

clue.text: False dawn finally admitted by United faithful

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is taken
someone admitted is let in, so this letter goes inside the other words

blocks.note: U is short for United, as in football club names
the final letter of dawn
true means loyal, faithful

explanation.surface: A misleading early recovery is finally conceded by loyal supporters of United.
explanation.walkthrough: A false dawn is a promising sign that comes to nothing; here 'False' is the definition and 'dawn' a letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue is incorrect or not in accordance with fact, so false.

clue.text: Start without a midday meal

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letter is taken away

blocks.note: to launch a project is to start it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Beginning the day with no meal at noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the meal eaten in the middle of the day, between breakfast and dinner.

clue.text: Take out language proceeding from fear at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so just the first letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the language spoken in Poland
of can mean coming from, as in 'a man of Kent'
the opening letter of fear

explanation.surface: A tongue that springs from dread at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' suggests removing something; here it is the slang for killing.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish someone off is slang for killing or defeating them, just as to take someone out is.

clue.text: Remain unfinished needing fellows in support

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to stay is to remain
F is short for fellow; doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Staying on with a job half done, needing colleagues for backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a stout stick used to lean on while walking, so a physical prop.

clue.text: Extremely volatile converted realist of many sided ability

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes, the two ends of the word
something converted is changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first and last letters of volatile
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A highly volatile realist who has been converted shows a talent for many things.
explanation.definitionFit: A versatile person can adapt to many different tasks or roles with skill.

clue.text: Site of siege and massacre a month after the French return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the French article reads backwards

blocks.note: la is French for the, feminine
taken as written
mo is an abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: A historic massacre site visited a month after French troops come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts a month after the turned-round French word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo, a mission in San Antonio, Texas, was besieged in 1836 and its defenders were killed by Mexican forces.

clue.text: Town’s bread maker

blocks.note: first meaning: a small historic town in East Sussex, England
second meaning: a cereal grain milled into flour for dark bread

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a town's baker; 'bread maker' is a grain, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a Cinque Port town in East Sussex, and rye is the grain used for rye bread and pumpernickel.

clue.text: Deus ex machina perhaps causing present outcome

blocks.note: to stage a play is to present it
an effect is a result

explanation.surface: A god lowered by machine produces the current outcome of a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Deus ex machina is Latin for 'god from the machine', a god winched onto the ancient stage to resolve a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical device such as a crane lowering a god is one example of a contrived piece of theatre spectacle.
